messages:
alerts-bot: :rotating_light: HOSTED-USW2 GPU_POOL 'hosted-usw2-pool-7' p95-queueing > 3.2s, admission throttle triggered (20% requests dropped). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/hosted-usw2/pool-7?orgId=1

maya: seeing the same in the dashboard. KV cache hit is down to 61%. prefix-cache miss rate jumped ~4x.

sam: @maya do we have an owner on this? Is this localized to pool-7 or across all hosted-usw2 pools?

maya: looks concentrated on pool-7 and its burst nodes. Other pools show a small uptick but under threshold. Correlates with a spike of long-seq generation jobs from a single tenant id: tenant_42.

olivia: oncall here — collecting logs: `kubectl logs -n serving pool-7-controller -c admission` shows repeated `eviction: insufficient compute` messages around 1919001200.

diego: could be noisy tenant with large seqs. Any change in routing config or rollout recently?

infra-bot: current pool sizes: pool-7=24 gpus (8 T4 burst nodes), pool-6=32, pool-8=24. Admission thresholds: p95-queue=2s, active-queues>100 triggers throttle. Active queue for pool-7=326.

maya: adding more details — recent batch: ~1200 requests/min with 20% > 2048 tokens. The runtime is failing to reuse KV cache because many unique prefixes (eval workloads).

sam: suggestion: temporarily raise admission hard-limit for pool-7 to keep latency under slos while we mitigate? We'll risk cost spike. Thoughts?

olivia: we should avoid blowing through burst capacity. Preferred: 1) route tenant_42 to dedicated-sandbox, 2) enable per-tenant rate-limiting to protect pool.

diego: I can flip a routing rule to divert tenant_42 to dedicated-sandbox-1: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/routing -d '{"tenant":"tenant_42","route":"dedicated-sandbox-1"}'` — will that break anything?

maya: route change looks safe for now. We'll need to ensure their model variant exists on sandbox. I'll check.

infra-bot: model-catalog check: tenant_42 uses open-gpt-v2-llama variant — present on dedicated-sandbox-1, but quantization differs (q4_0). Fallback available.

olivia: plan: 1) temporarily divert tenant_42 (diego) 2) increase admission limit by 10% for pool-7 for 5m (maya) 3) throttle long-seq requests by size for hosted (sam) 4) create incident record (olivia).

sam: I'm OK with diversion + short bump in admission. Who will create the incident ticket?

olivia: I'll open the ticket and assign P1 to eng-infra. Ticket: RED-INC-3421. Adding runbook note.

maya: executing admission bump: `redwoodctl pools update pool-7 --admission-threshold 2.2s --duration 300s` — applied at 1919001254.

diego: diversion command executed at 1919001265. `curl ...` returned 200. Routing now sends tenant_42 to dedicated-sandbox-1.

infra-bot: telemetry after changes (1919001270): pool-7 active queue -> 142, p95-queue -> 1.9s, KV hit -> 68%. Admission drops to 3%.

maya: observing backend latencies improving. Heap of small model restarts from prior evictions still draining but trending down.

sam: good. Can we add a short-term policy: if any tenant > 10% of pool qps AND 30% long-seq rate, auto-divert to a sandbox/dedicated pool?

olivia: we have a draft of that policy in runbook-ops. I'll PR a proposal to policy repo and add simulated checks. For now, add a watch alert.

diego: cost note — diverting to dedicated-sandbox uses reserved capacity; cost impact minimal for short window. If tenant doesn't reduce seq sizes we'll need quota enforcement.

maya: action items: 1) olivia create ticket (RED-INC-3421) & attach logs 2) sam to draft short-term rate-limit rule (size-based) 3) diego to keep routing in place for 30m and monitor 4) maya to follow KV cache analysis and suggest cache priming if needed.

olivia: ticket created and assigned. Adding root-cause placeholder: noisy long-sequence evals. Will update after postmortem.

sam: thumbs up. Follow-up: add a dashboard panel for per-tenant long-seq contribution so we surface this earlier.

maya: created dashboard panel prototype: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/hosted-usw2/per-tenant-longseq — feedback welcome.

infra-bot: final telemetry snapshot 1919001288: pool-7 active queue=98, p95=1.6s, admission throttle=0.9%.

diego: I'll hold diversion until 1919003065 (~30m) and then revert if stable.

maya: thanks all. closing this Slack thread — will update ticket with timeline and metrics. :white_check_mark:
